Context/Background: In a prospective endometrial carcinoma (EC) cohort, we performed a differential analysis of protein levels between hotspot-mutated CTNNB1 and WT CTNNB1 tumors, in the CNV-L subgroup.  In a separate analysis, we found that CTNNB1 S45 phosphorylation was significantly downregulated in hotspot-mutated tumors, whereas phosphosites distant from the hotspot mutations were mostly upregulated.
Prompt: Provide a discussion of the results from the differential analysis and any relevance to the mutation state of CTNNB1.

Introduction/Context  
In a CNV-L subgroup of endometrial carcinoma (EC) tumors, proteomic profiling (10,150 proteins quantified) compared hotspot-mutated CTNNB1 versus wild-type CTNNB1. 1,835 proteins were significantly altered (FDR < 0.05). Independently, CTNNB1 S45‐phosphorylation was found downregulated in hotspot mutants, whereas non-hotspot phosphosites trended upward (not shown here).

Key Differential Proteins  
• CTNNB1: log2 FC +0.760 (FDR 1.7 × 10⁻¹¹)  
• AXIN1: +0.672 (FDR 1.9 × 10⁻¹²)  
• DKK4: +4.05 (FDR 6.4 × 10⁻⁸)  
• LEF1: +1.31 (FDR 6.4 × 10⁻⁸)  
• LRP4: +1.55 (FDR 8.4 × 10⁻⁷)  

Functional Enrichment  
- GSEA preranked on all L2FCs identified WNT signaling among the top upregulated pathways:  
  – KEGG_2016 “Wnt signaling pathway” (NES 4.35, FDR q 6.9 × 10⁻⁴), leading‐edge genes DKK4, CTNNB1, AXIN1, LEF1, etc.  
  – MSigDB_Hallmark_2020 “Wnt-beta Catenin Signaling” (NES 3.40, FDR q 2.6 × 10⁻³).  
- ORA of the 778 upregulated proteins highlighted “Wnt-beta Catenin Signaling” (FDR 4.2 × 10⁻³).

Interpretation  
Hotspot CTNNB1 mutations drive increased abundance of core WNT/β-catenin pathway components (CTNNB1, LEF1, AXIN1) and feedback regulators (DKK4, LRP4), indicating pathway activation at the protein level. The downregulation of CTNNB1 S45 phosphorylation—normally a degradation signal—further supports stabilized β-catenin in mutant tumors. Elevated AXIN1 and DKK4 likely reflect engaged negative feedback loops, while upregulation of transcription factors (LEF1) and CTNNB1 itself denotes downstream target induction. Thus, CTNNB1 hotspot mutations in EC potentiate canonical WNT signaling, with implications for targeting this axis in CTNNB1-mutant tumors.

Next Steps & Clarification  
1. Phosphoproteome integration: quantify S45 versus other CTNNB1 phosphosites to map degradation versus activation dynamics.  
2. Functional assays: test WNT target gene expression (e.g., CCND1, MMP7) in matched tumors or cell lines.  
3. Therapeutic relevance: evaluate sensitivity of CTNNB1-mutant EC models to WNT/β-catenin inhibitors.  
4. Broader context: assess whether WNT activation correlates with clinical variables (stage, outcome) within CNV-L EC.

Key Themes Presence  
- Replication/cell-cycle: not directly assessed here (though GSEA flagged ribosome and mitochondrial gene expression).  
- Stress responses: UPR and protein-processing pathways were also enriched (secondary).  
- Metabolism/mitochondria: oxidative phosphorylation and mitochondrial translation emerged as strong upregulated themes in GSEA, suggesting network crosstalk with WNT signaling.
